analysis:
Examined ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift (base and head) and ToolConstraintSchema.swift (patch and base). No concrete security regression found.

ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy: GLM5NextPromptPolicy models are now routed to .structuredPostValidation (head lines 54-59). advertisesCapability (head 84-90) requires both GLM5NextPromptPolicy.applies and GLM5NextCoordinatorServing.isManagedModelID, so a model type alone does not advertise the capability. validateParser (head 165-171) requires the .glm5 format and fails closed otherwise, with an early return placed before the generic Qwen/Nemotron fallthrough. One asymmetry: forcedStrategy admits by modelType only, with no managed-ID check. However, advertisesCapability gates what is advertised and routed, and a forced choice for a non-advertised GLM model still goes through the withheld parse and schema validation path. This looks like capability gating rather than a bypass of fail-closed validation. Unverified: GLM5NextPromptPolicy.applies(modelType:), GLM5NextCoordinatorServing, the .glm5 ToolCallFormat and the actual withheld-validation implementation are outside the supplied source. The claims in the comments (GLM refuses sampler constraints, media refuses forced choice before media work) cannot be confirmed here. The next pass should confirm that GLM image/media requests with forced tool_choice are actually refused, because forcedStrategy admits GLM regardless of media. T-008-class risk (no unvalidated tool output exposed) depends on that withholding.

ToolConstraintSchema: compileResponseSchema now calls requireExplicitResponseTypes after compilation, so untyped response_format schemas are rejected. This is stricter, so it tightens the controls rather than weakening them. The recursion covers properties and items only, and compileSchema has already bounded depth and validated those positions, so there is no unbounded-recursion concern. A nullable type array, such as ["string","null"], counts as typed. Schemas whose only content is an unsupported keyword are rejected earlier by compileSchema. Availability impact is limited to rejecting some previously accepted untyped schemas.

No threat-model assets or trust boundaries involving keys, attestation, the cache or billing are touched.
